explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/757: Gyárfás–Lehel [GyLe95] proved 1/2 + 1/(141·76) ≤ c ≤ 3/5 (the upper bound from the first n Fibonacci numbers), and Ma–Tang [MaTa26] improved this to 9/17 ≤ c ≤ 4/7. The Lean IsAdmissible c says every finite A ⊆ ℝ whose 4-subsets B all satisfy |B−B| ≥ 11 contains a Sidon subset of size ≥ c|A|; the set of admissible c is downward closed (c ≤ 0 trivially) and bounded, so sSup is the "best constant". The theorem asserts sSup < 3/5 (strict). This strict form is true given the Ma–Tang bound c ≤ 4/7, but the docstring attributes it to [GyLe95], which per the source only gives ≤ 3/5 — a non-strict bound would not yield the stated strict inequality from GyLe95 alone. Minor issues: the docstring misattribution/strictness and an unused binder {A : Set ℝ}. The mathematical statement itself is a correct, proved consequence of the literature, so severity 2.
